title: Cleaning and sanitising waste bins
audience: Cleaners who wash the interior and exterior of waste bins on a scheduled basis.
learningOutcomes: Choose between a light clean and a heavy clean for a waste bin based on the soil present.
Remove crusted matter before applying a cleaning solution, and apply the product at the label strength.
Dry and reline a bin before returning it to service.

instruction.heading: When a bin needs more than a wipe
instruction.body: Most bins need only an outside wipe at each visit. A bin needs a deeper clean when residue has built up inside, when it smells, or when a spill has dried onto the surface. Decide first whether the soil is light or heavy, because that choice sets the method.

instruction.heading: Light soil
instruction.body: Take the bin to the cleaning area and mist both the interior and the exterior with a sanitising solution made up to the label. Dry it off with a cotton rag or kitchen paper. Check the seams and the base, where residue tends to collect.

instruction.heading: Heavy soil
instruction.body: Scrape hard, crusted matter from the inside with a putty knife first, so the solution can reach the surface. Fill the bin with cleaning solution at the strength on the label and leave it to soak for the time the label gives. Scrub using a nylon brush or a green scrub pad. A melamine sponge can lift marks, but use it lightly on painted or glossy surfaces. Rinse, then dry the inside completely before reuse.

instruction.heading: Returning the bin
instruction.body: Fit a fresh liner and seat it, then return the bin to its place on the route. A bin that goes back damp develops odour and leaves wet rings on the floor and the liner.

procedure: Remove the liner and empty the bin into the collection bin.
Take the bin to the cleaning area.
If the soil is heavy, scrape off crusted matter with a putty knife.
Light soil: spray, wipe and dry. Heavy soil: soak at label strength, scrub, rinse and dry.
Dry the inside completely, fit a liner, and return the bin to its place.

workedExamples.situation: A bin in the kitchen area has a sticky ring of spilled soft drink dried onto its base.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which method should be used, and what precautions apply?
workedExamples.reasoning: This is heavy soil. Scrape first, then soak at the label strength, scrub the base using a nylon brush, rinse and dry. Wear eye protection and gloves. Use one product at a time and do not mix it with another. If the label does not allow the product on that plastic, choose a different product or ask the site contact.

equipmentAndPpe: Sanitiser spray bottle and cleaning solution at label strength
Nylon brush and green scrub pad

commonErrors.error: Mixing two cleaning products in one bin.
commonErrors.prevention: Use one product at a time and rinse between products. Never combine them.

commonErrors.error: Returning the bin to service while it is still wet.
commonErrors.prevention: Dry the inside before the liner goes back in.

commonErrors.error: Scratching the bin with metal tools.
commonErrors.prevention: Use a plastic scraper or nylon brush, and test on a hidden spot first.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Do not combine products. Follow the label and the safety data sheet for each product in use.
Wear eye protection and gloves when scrubbing, soaking or spraying.

qualityStandard: Both the interior and the exterior of the bin are clean and dry.
No residue remains at the seams, the base or the rim.
A fresh liner is fitted before the bin returns to service.
documentationEvidence: Heavy-soil bins recorded on the site record for follow-up.
summary: Decide on light or heavy soil first, and choose the method to match.
Scrape crusted matter before soaking, and use the product at label strength.
Dry the bin fully before a liner goes back in.

knowledgeChecks.question: What should be done before soaking a bin with crusted matter?
options: Scrape the crusted matter off first so the solution can reach the surface
Pour a second product straight in and leave it to foam up quickly
Fill it with water only and leave it for a day before the next shift

knowledgeChecks.question: Why must a bin be dried inside before a liner goes back in?
options: Wet bins are impossible to carry and the liners tear easily
A damp bin is more likely to develop odour and wet rings
Dry bins are the only kind the site accepts on this route

knowledgeChecks.question: Which tool is the safer choice for the inside of a bin?
options: A steel wool pad for scrubbing
A stiff wire brush for scrubbing
A plastic scraper or a nylon brush

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the lesson say to decide first when a bin needs more than a wipe?
options: How many bins are on the route
Whether the soil is light or heavy
